purpose: Inputs and reference values for a 3-D near-field simulation of what a pedestrian breathes beside idling petrol scooters at a red light, and for its fair comparisons. Source ids refer to research/estimate/sources.json (existing) or research/simulation/sources.json (new). status: V = opened and figure found in the source by this job or a prior verified project file; S = secondary (figure read in another document, or an abstract only); D = derived here by stated arithmetic; A = assumption with basis.
integrityNote: No value in this file was chosen to reach or avoid any guideline. Where a source gives a range, the whole range is given. The owner expects the result to exceed a guideline; this file records what the sources say, including the facts that point both ways (odour thresholds are reached at dilutions where CO is far below WHO values, AND strong exhaust odour can coincide with momentary CO of tens of ppm; enclosed car parks DO exceed the WHO 15-min CO value).

unitConversions.averaging_rule: A level C held for t seconds and zero (above background) otherwise contributes C*t/T to a T-second mean: a 90 s red at C adds C/10 to a 15-min mean and C/40 to a 1-h mean; 10 consecutive 90-s reds within 15 min (impossible with 120-200 s cycles) would be needed for a 90-s level to equal the 15-min mean. With a cycle of 120-180 s and the person waiting only one red, the 15-min mean is about (90/900)*C_red + background.

tailpipe.summary: Warm idle of an in-use 100-150 cc four-stroke scooter: exhaust about 0.3-0.8 L/s (STP, central 0.47) leaving a 18-32 mm pipe at 0.3-0.5 m height, about 150-350 C (assumed; no idle measurement found), so 0.5-6 m/s exit velocity and a weak buoyancy flux of order 1e-3 to 8e-3 m4/s3. Raw idle CO: inspection distribution with 75 % of tests in the 0-1 % bin, 25 % >= 1 %, 6.7 % >= 3 %, 1.5 % >= 5 %. Raw HC 370-530 ppm (hexane, NDIR) for ordinary phases, about 5,800 ppm for the failing tail and about 5,400 ppm for two-strokes. Raw benzene 12-33 ppm for four-strokes and 83-116 ppm for two-strokes (Bangkok, 100-150 cc).

items.basis: Measured: four-stroke CVT motorcycle idle exhaust 'very low flow rate ~30 L/min' (Vojtisek-Lom 2020, V; ~20 L/min for a 50 cc moped). Carbon balance: fuel F = 80/120/200 g/h (estimate input), 0.86 gC/g, carbon species 12.5 % of exhaust moles -> 0.31/0.47/0.78 L/s at 25 C. Engine physics: 125 cc x 1700 rpm / 2 = 1.77 L/s swept, idle volumetric efficiency 0.2-0.35 -> 0.35-0.62 L/s (A).

items.basis: No measured warm-idle exit temperature for a scooter was found. Bounds: exhaust rose from 25 to 200-300 C within 3 min of cold start on a motorcycle PEMS test (Vojtisek-Lom 2020, V, not idle-specific); idle sampling protocol required >= 50 C at the pipe end after 10 min warm-up (Rungratanaubon 2007, V, a lower bound); CG125 tailpipe gas maximum 306 C over 1000-5000 rpm (Ghafori 2016, V, idle not tested). Buoyancy is a minor term for receptors > 0.5 m away (estimate sensitivity: no buoyant rise changed median < 5 %), but it decides whether the plume core passes pushchair height within 1 m; the simulation should test 100-350 C.

nearField.summary: No measurement of concentration versus distance 0.3-3 m behind an idling scooter exists in anything opened. Usable anchors: moving-car plumes diluted ~6,000x by 3 m (Toronto); a diesel pickup's PM at stroller height (0.85 m) ~1.6x (mean) to 1.8x (1.5-s peak) adult mouth height (1.65 m) at 0.75 m lateral; kerb NO2 +5-15 % at 0.8 m vs 2.0 m within 2.5 m of the kerb and no difference beyond; in-pram particles up to +44 %; Ning 2005: idle plumes decay exponentially in all directions, and a 15-deg exit angle keeps the plume near the ground. A UC Riverside 2024 field test measured CO2 at 1-6 m behind an idling truck at 1-4 m heights (values in figures only).

a 25 mm jet at 1.7 m/s has momentum length scale ~ d*sqrt(rho_j/rho_a) ~ 2 cm and becomes wind- or wake-dominated within ~0.1-0.3 m; near-field mixing at 0.3-3 m is set by ambient turbulence (sigma_v 0.2-0.5 m/s floor in the estimate), the scooter/rider wake (none when stationary, CAL3QHC) and weak buoyancy

Taiwan 1989-91 (two-stroke era, mixed traffic): Taipei roadside and arcade (corridor) CO 7.8-8.3 ppm mean of 30-60 min samples, maxima 40 ppm (arcade, 60 min) and 101 ppm (roadside, 30-50 min); bus stops 13 ppm mean, 42 max; on motorcycles 17.5 mean, 126 max. Elsewhere: Hanoi walking 8.5 ppm (2006); HCMC intersections daily 1.7-8.7 ppm, max hourly ~20 (S); Bangkok motorcycle commuters 12.8 ppm (S).

enclosedCases.summary: Enclosed car parks are the one documented everyday setting where CO above the WHO 15-min value occurs: in 52 Hong Kong underground car parks (1990s, cars) the 15-min TWA averaged 39 ppm and reached 362 ppm, 1-min maxima averaged 98 ppm (9-667), and > 34 % failed WHO-type criteria; Beirut underground parking peaks 26-140 mg/m3 (30-min). Taipei's 60 underground car parks name CO as the main parking-area pollutant (no values in abstract). No measurement of CO under a Taiwanese arcade beside a scooter queue, in a covered scooter waiting zone, or in a tunnel carrying scooters was found; Taiwanese tunnel studies opened exclude motorcycles.

items.value: 52 underground car parks, peak hours, sensor at 1.5 m: 1-min max 9-667 ppm (mean 98); 5-min TWA 6.4-506.6 (mean 59); 15-min TWA 3-361.6 (mean 39); 30-min TWA 2.7-255.1 (mean 32); 1-h TWA 2-153.8 (mean 25); highest at ramps (low gear, queuing)

Well-mixed enclosure: C = N q / Q_air. With q = 15 g/h per idling scooter (fleet mean, 4.2 mg/s) and 100 mg/m3: Q_air <= N x 0.042 m3/s. 30 idling scooters need less than 1.3 m3/s of fresh air through the space they share, e.g. a 3 m x 3.5 m arcade cross-section ventilated at < 0.12 m/s, or an enclosed 300 m3 waiting room at < 15 air changes per hour, held for 15 min. Outdoors the street's air exchange is tens to hundreds of m3/s, so a 15-min mean of 87 ppm would need a sealed or near-sealed volume, emitters far above the fleet mean, or both.

odour.summary: Odour is the comparison that matches 'it smelled horrible'. Whole petrol-engine exhaust is detectable at roughly 800 to 6,800-fold dilution of raw exhaust (two independent 1967-70 panel studies, abstracts). Gasoline vapour headspace: detection 0.47-0.58 ppm, recognition 0.77-1.12 ppm (API 1995). Key odorants by Nagata triangle-bag detection threshold (ppm): acetaldehyde 0.0015, propionaldehyde 0.0010, n-butyraldehyde 0.00067, isovaleraldehyde 0.00010, acrolein 0.0036, crotonaldehyde 0.023, formaldehyde 0.50, H2S 0.00041, methyl mercaptan 0.000070, dimethyl sulfide 0.0030, carbonyl sulfide 0.055, SO2 0.87, NO2 0.12, styrene 0.035, m-xylene 0.041, p-xylene 0.058, ethylbenzene 0.17, toluene 0.33, o-xylene 0.38, 1-butene 0.36, 1,3-butadiene 0.23, 1-pentene 0.10, n-heptane 0.67, isooctane 0.67, isopentane 1.3, n-pentane 1.4, n-hexane 1.5, benzene 2.7, 2-methylpentane 7.0, 3-methylpentane 8.9, isobutene 10, propylene 13, acetone 42. CO is odourless. Individual thresholds vary ~5x between repeated panels (Nagata), more across people.
odour.howQuantified: Odour concentration = the dilution factor at which 50 % of a panel (6-10 assessors) detect the sample (dilution-to-threshold, D/T; European odour unit ouE/m3 = number of dilutions to threshold). A sample diluted 100 times to threshold is 100 OU/m3 (Danish EPA). For a mixture, a first estimate is the sum of odour activity values OAV_i = C_i / OT_i (an approximation; mixtures are often sub-additive). For whole exhaust: OU at the nose ~ (D/T of raw exhaust) / (dilution from tailpipe to nose).

items.value: odour threshold expressed as log10(dilution factor): 3.72-3.83 for gasoline engines with different emission controls (D/T 5,200-6,800), 3.17 for uncontrolled diesel at idle (D/T 1,500); idle and ECE cycle intensities of the same order

items.value: If raw scooter exhaust has D/T ~800-6,800 and raw CO 0.5-5 %, then at exactly the odour threshold the CO increment is 0.7-60 ppm (central ~2-20 ppm). A 'horrible' smell (say 5-30x threshold) implies dilution of ~30-1,400, i.e. momentary CO of ~4 to >1,000 ppm in that puff (wide). Because odour depends on HC/aldehydes, a rich, HC-heavy scooter (or two-stroke) smells at much higher dilution than its CO alone would suggest. This links smell to momentary plume hits, not to 15-min means.

fairComparisonNotes: Seconds-to-minutes peaks: the only CO values with averaging times of 10-15 min are the WHO 15-min guideline (87 ppm) and AEGL-2 10-min (420 ppm, a disabling-effects emergency level, not a public-health guideline). NIOSH's 200 ppm ceiling is occupational and instantaneous. There is no AEGL-1 for CO. A 1-s or 10-s peak must not be compared with these without averaging over their window.
A 90-s red contributes C_red/10 to a 15-min mean if the rest of the 15 min is at background; a 15-min mean of 87 ppm from one red would need C_red ~ 870 ppm sustained for 90 s at the nose.
For benzene and aldehydes, the 1-h OEHHA acute RELs are the shortest health-based values; a 90-s level contributes C/40 to a 1-h mean. Annual and lifetime values are not fair comparisons.
Odour comparisons have a seconds averaging time and are fair against second-by-second simulated concentrations; they speak to perception, not to toxicity.
gaps: No measured warm-idle exit temperature or outlet diameter for a Taiwanese scooter (assumed 150-350 C, 18-32 mm).
No measurement of concentration versus distance 0.3-3 m behind an idling scooter; Ding et al. 2023 (APR) still blocked; Ning 2005 and TTI 2024 give no usable numbers in text.
No idle aldehyde or sulphur-compound emission measurement for scooters; odour estimate must use cycle speciation and whole-exhaust D/T from 1967-70 car engines.
Whole-exhaust D/T values are from abstracts in an EPA translation bibliography, not the original papers.

No CO measurement under a Taiwanese arcade beside a scooter queue (the 1989-91 Liu corridor data are whole-traffic), in a covered scooter waiting zone, or in a tunnel/underground car park with scooters (Taipei 60-lot study gives no values in abstract).
No 1990s pedestrian CO number for Italy or India was opened; Delhi data located but not read.
Taiwan ambient CO 1-h standard: 31 ppm (2024 amendment as printed in the MOENV annual report) vs 35 ppm in older sources; law text not re-opened.
Pull-away burst at green unquantified for scooters.
